text:
Ishaan: quick concept drop: 'channeling' patches — instead of per-shard deltas, tag patches with channel ids (e.g. embeddings, kv-cache, blocks-0-5) and stream/apply per-channel. channeling lets router and warmup control granularity without changing safetensors on-disk format.

Priya: sounds promising. how are channels discovered? manifest extension?

Ishaan: yes, manifest gets a channels list with map of scope->channel-id and per-channel patch entries. e.g. channels: [{id:emb,regex:embeddings.*},{id:block0_5,regex:blocks.0-5.*}] then patches reference channel ids.

Luca: runtime-wise: overlay namespace per-channel. lookup order: channel-overlay -> base-shard. still keeps safetensors blobs as-is.

Tess: warmup implication: router needs channel readiness. can we expose readiness per-channel (bool/percent) so traffic can be split?

Ishaan: propose /bundle/<id>/status returns channel readiness map and channel-level progress (percentage). Router can circuit-break or send probes based on that.

Priya: atomicity risk: multi-channel commit must be consistent. what if channel A commits but B fails?

Luca: use a two-phase commit: stage overlays for all channels, verify checksums, then flip active pointer in one atomic step. if verify fails rollback staged overlays. staged overlays have lease TTL so GC is automatic.

Tess: security: manifest signature must cover channels and patch digests. also per-patch signature helps. restrict channel regex to allowed patterns.

Ishaan: rollout plans: canary by channel and by replica percentage. manifest patch entry can include rollout:{type:percent, pct:10, channels:["emb"]}. start with embeddings-only canaries.

Priya: metrics to add: channel_apply_ms, channel_readiness_pct, staged_overlay_mem_bytes, channel_quarantine_count. also tracing spans per-channel.

Luca: perf PoC: base 10GB, emb-channel patch 200MB. measure apply latency, peak mem, and percent of requests that hit fallback during partial apply.

bridge-bot: RFC stub created: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/staged-delta-channeling (Ishaan)
